SEC sues crypto lender Nimbus, alleging $1.2 billion fraud

Published 2026-10-06 15:40 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday sued crypto lender Nimbus Lending and its CEO Mark Ellery, alleging the firm defrauded more than 90,000 retail investors out of $1.2 billion.

According to the SEC, Nimbus marketed its Yield Vault product as a safe way to earn up to 14% a year by lending crypto to institutions, but it paid earlier investors with deposits from newer ones. The complaint also alleges Ellery took more than $40 million for himself.

Nimbus froze withdrawals in August. A lawyer for Ellery said he would fight the charges. The case is one of the largest crypto enforcement actions brought by the SEC this year, and bitcoin slipped about 2% after the news.
